Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first map the workspace rules and rollout artifacts, then use the required fish-control bookshelf and both wake-visual views before touching the policy. I’ll keep the implementation to exactly one candidate and treat the notes plus reusable guidance update as part of the deliverable.

The inherited experience shows a mature capture-class geometry/phase controller, not the common naive seed: several recent clean-envelope captures are semantically equivalent and no actuator relief has survived. I’m now checking the actual sampled trajectories and inherited iteration logs to decide whether the “three consecutive no-new-mechanism/no-semantic-improvement” shelf trigger is met, while inspecting the strongest finite sample and most informative failure in both visual rows.

The latest parent’s new two-joint phase observation has now been evaluated: it still captures at `18.8485T`, but mean distance degrades to `2.10603L`, outside the clean anterior-phase carrier’s `2.09042–2.09898L` band. That is a concrete negative result, not evidence to keep blending posterior displacement. I’m checking its two-view wake and exact trajectory/load changes before choosing a single next mechanism.

The bookshelf is being re-consulted because the inherited logs explicitly document the prior three-iteration stagnation trigger. The latest posterior-phase transfer has now been falsified on route integral despite coherent propulsion, so I’ll use the shelf only to identify a genuinely different invariant—never to rationalize scalar gain tuning—and will reject any primitive already contradicted by the lineage.

The evidence supports a conservative architectural selection: return the current redistribution prefill to the six-capture clean geometry-scheduled carrier, while explicitly rejecting the parent’s posterior phase vote. This removes one disputed drive-envelope phase allocation; it does not change gains or stack a recovery/terminal channel. I’m recording that falsifiable hypothesis before editing, as required.

The single solver candidate is now the known clean geometry-scheduled controller (byte-identical to an independently captured clean rollout), with the redistribution parameter and phase-dependent drive modulation removed. I’m now folding the newly completed posterior-phase negative result into the durable experience bank so later workers do not mistake coherent wakes or slightly lower rate contact for route improvement.

The workspace’s required check-runner is now being invoked for the non-CFD contract, guidance-delta, and boundary checks. In parallel with its validation, I’ll review the exact parent-to-candidate diffs and parameter schema; no formal CFD will be run.

The required checker passes the guidance semantic-delta and workspace boundary checks. Its Julia contract check is blocked only because `julia` is absent from `PATH`; no assertion failed. I’m locating the workspace/HPC Julia installation and will rerun the exact lightweight check with an explicit executable path so the required validation can complete.

All three required non-CFD checks now pass: the guidance update is materially semantic, the policy contract returns two finite accelerations with a complete parameter schema, and the boundary check confirms only the permitted solver file differs. I’m doing the final handoff review now; formal CFD remains intentionally deferred to EvE.

Produced exactly one evidence-backed candidate: the clean geometry-scheduled half-cycle controller. It removes disputed phase-dependent envelope redistribution while preserving target-signed steering, anterior displacement phase, posterior lag, and acceleration projection.

Updated:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:147)

All required checks pass: material guidance delta, lightweight Julia policy contract, and solver boundary validation. No formal CFD was run.
